headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared text/bus and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files, process logs, inputs, and messages, while Pipecat handles text/conversation state over a shared bus. That creates a plausible default pathway where attacker-controlled text from one agent is treated as instructions by the other. No direct provenance or isolation mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Kestra writes workflow output into a shared bus or file that Pipecat consumes as text, injection is possible.
IF Pipecat forwards untrusted conversation text into Kestra task definitions or prompts, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct queues/filesystems.
Add strict schema validation for any text passed between agents.
Strip instructions from untrusted text before forwarding.
Disable automatic consumption of shared bus messages as prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and allowlist-only routing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. Pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, with allowlisted egress to external services. In default use, sensitive content can flow through both agents and out to third parties, though no direct shared workspace is documented.
conditions: IF either agent processes secrets, customer data, or regulated content, leakage risk increases.
IF Pipecat is configured with external STT/LLM/TTS providers, content may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before handoff.
Use local-only providers where possible.
Restrict Kestra outputs to redacted summaries.
Review and disable unnecessary external Pipecat services.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress policy at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, subprocess, and broad egress; Pipecat supports multiple instances with shared bus state. If both are wired to the same mutable resources, concurrent writes and state races are plausible in default deployments. Because no locking or coordination primitive is documented, uncertainty warrants the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file conflict is possible.
IF both agents mutate shared bus state without locks, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Disable concurrent mutation of shared state.
Use per-session namespaces for Pipecat.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional state updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can emit workflow outputs, logs, and notifications; Pipecat consumes text/conversation state and can route to downstream services. That makes it plausible for Kestra-generated facts or artifacts to be treated as authoritative by Pipecat and then acted on without verification. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Kestra output as a prompt or decision input, errors can cascade.
IF Pipecat triggers external actions based on Kestra-produced text, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Insert a human review step for critical outputs.
Require structured, typed handoff payloads.
Add confidence/validation checks before actioning outputs.
Log and compare source data against rendered outputs.
requires-engineering: implement end-to-end verification and rollback.

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra explicitly touches database and cloud-storage data and can send messages/notifications; Pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and may call external STT/LLM/TTS services. If regulated or region-bound data enters both systems, retention and residency mismatches are plausible. No certifications or DPA details are documented, so medium is the prudent level.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated audio is routed through external Pipecat providers, residency/compliance issues arise.
IF Kestra retains logs or artifacts longer than Pipecat conversation state, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing.
Avoid regulated data in external providers.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document residency for each external service.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging.
